newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Former Venezuelan president launches new party.
newsitem.headline: Former Venezuelan president launches new party.

text.p: Former Venezuelan President Carlos Andres Perez, the only Latin American leader to be jailed for corruption, launched a new political party on Thursday to challenge the traditional party structure he helped create.
About 2,500 supporters of the two-time president cheered Perez as he announced the creation of the "Movement for Openness and National Participation" -- his new party.
"We are born with a vocation for power," Perez told the partisan crowd gathered at a luxury hotel in Caracas.
Perez, 73, was forced out of office in May 1993, just eight months short of completing his second five-year mandate, on charges of misusing state funds.

After serving more than two years of house arrest in September 1996 -- following two months in a low-security El Junquito jail in Caracas -- he was stripped of the lifelong Senate position awarded former presidents and kicked out of the party he helped form 50 years ago.

One of Latin America's most flamboyant politicians, Perez took swipes at his old party Democratic Action (AD), Venezuela's largest opposition party. "I am still the fundamental leader of AD," he said to roars of approval.
Perez, who survived bloody protests and two coup attempts in his last term, would be ineligible to run in Venezuela's next presidential elections in 1998.

Party sources tipped his former Planning Minister Miguel Rodriguez -- whose tough economic reforms were blamed by analysts for provoking the 1989 riots and 1992 military putsches -- as the party's likely candidate.
"We shall return to power!" Rodriguez shouted during his speech.
Perez intends to recover his place in Venezuelan politics by winning back the Senate seat for his birth state Tachira in western Venezuela.
